title: Diagnostic accuracy and feasibility of EXhaled Breath Aerosol (XBA) sampling for detection of respiratory PATHogens in symptomatic patients (B-Path symptomatic)
summary:
Respiratory infections are a leading cause of health problems globally. Testing for the presence of respiratory infections is important in order to correctly identify the cause and initiate appropriate management. Current diagnostic methods are limited by difficulty in sample collection and accuracy of pathogen detection. 

Human breath is an easy to obtain and non-invasive sample, and offers promise as a sample type for respiratory infection diagnostic tests. This study will use a face mask based breath collection device 

The study will look at how feasible, acceptable, and useable the face mask breath collection device is. Adult patients with symptoms of respiratory infections presenting to ambulatory clinics and emergency room departments in Heidelberg (Germany), Milan (Italy) and Bucharest (Romania) will be screened for inclusion in the study. Those eligible and consenting will provide one nasal swab and one breath sample using a face mask breath collection device. All participants will be offered the usual care and testing for respiratory infections provided by the clinic as per local guidelines. Nasal swab and breath samples will be tested for respiratory pathogens by PCR. We will assess how often the pathogens are detected, look at how many tests are successfully completed with the device, look at how many participants found the device easy to use, and understand how the breath test compares to current diagnostic tests.
conditions: Acute upper respiratory infections of multiple and unspecified sites

interventions.name: Participants will provide one nasal/nasopharyngeal swab and a breath sample using a mask-based breath collection device. Samples will be tested for respiratory pathogens using multiplex molecular platform(s).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients will be included for the first objective of the study if they meet the following criteria:

• adults (≥18 years of age) seeking care for respiratory symptoms at ambulatory clinic or emergency department sites 
• Symptoms of an Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI)  (e.g., cough, fever, shortness of breath, sore throat, coryza, rhinorrhoea)
• Able and willing to provide informed consent

For the secondary objectives, additional inclusion criteria are:

• Healthcare workers or related stakeholders for the respiratory diagnosis process
• Patients enrolled in the main study who have used the face mask sampling device in this study
• Provide consent to being interviewed and recorded
Exclusion criteria:
• Unable or unwilling to provide any reference standard samples (NPS)
• ARI symptoms lasting >10 days
• Unable or unwilling to provide informed consent
